title: [Theme/UI]: Authentic 1982 Commodore 64 VIC-II Palette & PETSCII Font Aesthetic Studio
body:
## Problem
ArcadeVerse's theme engine supports modern neon and vaporwave styles, but lacks an authentic recreation of the most iconic 8-bit computer in history: the 1982 Commodore 64, with its legendary 16-color VIC-II palette and PETSCII border aesthetics.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/theme-c64.css`:
   - Complete 16-color VIC-II palette variables: Light Blue (`#887ecb`), Classic Dark Blue (`#40318d`), Cyan (`#70a4b2`), Brown (`#683808`), Light Green (`#9ad284`), etc.
   - CRT 320x200 pixel aspect ratio simulation with authentic thick border letterboxing.
   - Custom monospace PETSCII-inspired font stack and flashing block cursor.
   - Retro READY. prompt styling on header elements.
2. Create modular studio controller `assets/js/theme-c64.js`:
   - Register theme with `ThemeStudio` or custom theme switcher under ID `commodore-64`.
   - Provide toggleable CRT raster scanlines and NTSC color bleeding artifacts.
   - Synthesize authentic C64 startup beep tone via Web Audio API when theme is engaged.
3. 100% Vanilla JS/CSS3. Zero npm packages, zero external fonts/CDNs.
4. Add standalone test file `scripts/test-theme-c64.js` validating color contrast, theme token registration, and scanline toggle logic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] C64 theme applies full 16-color VIC-II palette, border styling, and PETSCII aesthetics cleanly across the application.
- [ ] Theme registers smoothly into theme studio and persists in `localStorage`.
- [ ] Scanlines toggle dynamically without performance drop.
- [ ] Automated test `scripts/test-theme-c64.js` passes with 0 errors under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/VFX]: Interactive 2D Water Surface Wave Ripple & Specular Refraction Canvas Sandbox
body:
## Problem
ArcadeVerse features static canvas backdrops, but lacks interactive fluid wave physics simulations where user cursor gestures and clicks generate realistic propagating wave interference patterns and specular light refraction.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/water-ripples.css`:
   - Fullscreen interactive canvas container and retro arcade control HUD with damping, tension, and rain drop frequency sliders.
2. Create modular physics engine `assets/js/water-ripples.js`:
   - Implement discrete 2D wave equation on dual grid buffers (previous and current heightfields).
   - Propagate wave energy each frame: `height[x, y] = (h[x-1,y] + h[x+1,y] + h[x,y-1] + h[x,y+1]) / 2 - prev_h[x, y]`, multiplied by damping factor.
   - Render surface with normal map calculation, simulated specular light reflection, and underwater caustic refraction.
   - Support cursor dragging (continuous wave generator), clicking (splash drop), and automated ambient rain drops mode.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/HTML5 Canvas API. Zero external math or physics engines.
4. Add automated unit test `scripts/test-water-ripples.js` verifying buffer swapping, damping decay, and heightfield clamping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 2D wave equation propagates smooth, realistic water ripples across canvas at 60 FPS.
- [ ] Clicking and dragging on canvas triggers dynamic wave splashes.
- [ ] Physics parameters (damping, tension, rain speed) can be tuned in real-time.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-water-ripples.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Audio]: Dynamic 8-Bit Chiptune Arpeggiator & Chords Generator Using Web Audio API
body:
## Problem
Retro arcade games rely heavily on classic 8-bit chiptune music characterized by rapid arpeggios that simulated multi-voice polyphony on limited sound chips (NES 2A03, Game Boy DMG). ArcadeVerse lacks a procedural in-browser chiptune arpeggiator engine.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/chiptune-arpeggiator.css`:
   - Interactive synthesizer HUD with chord selectors (Major, Minor, Diminished, Pentatonic, 7th), octave controls, BPM dial, and waveform toggles (Square, Pulse 12.5%, Triangle, Noise).
2. Create modular audio engine `assets/js/chiptune-arpeggiator.js`:
   - Build procedural arpeggiator using Web Audio API `AudioContext` and scheduled oscillator nodes.
   - Implement precise rhythmic scheduling (`context.currentTime` based timeline) preventing audio drift.
   - Support arpeggio patterns: Up, Down, Up-Down, Random, and Fast Chord Strum (30Hz pseudo-polyphony).
   - Include visual retro audio oscilloscope canvas displaying the output square wave in real-time.
3. 100% Vanilla JS/Web Audio API. Zero external audio libraries (no Tone.js/Howler.js).
4. Add automated test file `scripts/test-chiptune-arpeggiator.js` validating note frequency calculation, chord formula intervals, and scheduling math.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Procedural arpeggiator generates crisp 8-bit chiptune melodies across multiple scales and waveforms.
- [ ] Real-time oscilloscope visualizes output audio wave smoothly.
- [ ] Tempo (BPM), octave, and chord parameters update dynamically without audio glitching.
- [ ] Test `scripts/test-chiptune-arpeggiator.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Graphics]: Procedural 2D Raymarched Metaball Liquid Blob Fusion Canvas Visualizer
body:
## Problem
Dynamic fluid blob visual effects (metaballs) are iconic in vintage demoscene and arcade intros, where smooth organic merging of circular fields creates liquid droplet illusions. ArcadeVerse lacks a dedicated procedural metaball canvas visualizer.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/metaball-visualizer.css`:
   - Canvas container with retro cyber controls for ball count, attraction force, threshold cutoff, and color gradient modes (Neon Lava, Cyber Acid, Liquid Mercury).
2. Create modular graphics engine `assets/js/metaball-visualizer.js`:
   - Implement scalar field function: for each pixel/sample point, compute $\sum (R_i^2 / d_i^2)$.
   - Apply thresholding and smooth step color mapping to generate crisp glowing liquid edges.
   - Simulate physics motion for 8-15 autonomous bouncing metaballs with velocity, gravity bounce, and cursor gravitational attraction.
   - Optimize rendering with downscaled buffer sampling or marching squares contouring to maintain steady 60 FPS.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/HTML5 Canvas. Zero external graphics libraries (no Three.js/Pixi.js).
4. Add automated test `scripts/test-metaball-visualizer.js` testing scalar field distance evaluation, boundary reflection, and color gradient interpolation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Metaballs fuse and separate smoothly with organic liquid surface tension.
- [ ] Interactive controls adjust ball count, threshold, and color gradients in real-time.
- [ ] High-performance rendering maintains smooth 60 FPS on standard desktop displays.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-metaball-visualizer.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Physics]: Interactive 2D Cloth & Soft-Body Mesh Verlet Integration Physics Engine
body:
## Problem
ArcadeVerse features particle effects, but lacks realistic soft-body and cloth physics simulations where users can interactively tear, drag, pin, and cut structural mesh networks.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/cloth-physics.css`:
   - Interactive canvas workbench with controls for cloth tension, gravity, wind intensity, and tool selector (Drag Hand, Scissor Cutter, Pin/Unpin).
2. Create modular physics engine `assets/js/cloth-physics.js`:
   - Implement Verlet integration particle system: `x_{new} = 2x - x_{old} + a \cdot dt^2`.
   - Structural constraint relaxation loops resolving particle spring distances and tearing thresholds.
   - Interactive mouse tools:
     - Drag Tool: Pull particles with dynamic spring tension.
     - Cut Tool: Sever spring constraints intersecting cursor trajectory to shred cloth.
     - Pin Tool: Lock particles in place to hang banners or curtains.
   - Simulated sinusoidal wind force blowing through mesh.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas API. Zero physics engines (no Matter.js/Phaser).
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-cloth-physics.js` verifying Verlet integration step math, constraint satisfaction, and constraint tearing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 2D cloth grid drapes and ripples realistically under gravity and simulated wind.
- [ ] Users can drag, pin, and cut cloth strands with interactive mouse tools.
- [ ] Performance remains stable at 60 FPS during heavy mesh deformations.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-cloth-physics.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Audio]: Dynamic Interactive Web Audio Dual-Oscillator FM Synthesizer Studio
body:
## Problem
Classic arcade sound chips like the Yamaha YM2151 and YM2612 (found in Sega Genesis and arcade boards) generated their iconic metallic, bell, and punchy bass sounds using Frequency Modulation (FM) synthesis. ArcadeVerse lacks an interactive FM synthesis laboratory.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/fm-synth-studio.css`:
   - Retro modular synthesizer interface with knobs/sliders for Carrier Frequency, Modulator Frequency, Modulation Index, and ADSR envelope (Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release).
   - Real-time XY touchpad control for simultaneous frequency and harmonic ratio morphing.
2. Create modular audio engine `assets/js/fm-synth-studio.js`:
   - Build dual-oscillator FM graph using Web Audio API: Modulator Oscillator $\rightarrow$ Modulator Gain Node $\rightarrow$ Carrier Oscillator Frequency parameter $\rightarrow$ Master Output Gain Node.
   - Implement factory presets: "Arcade Slap Bass", "Metallic Bell", "Laser Zap", "Cyber Chime", and "Retro Brass".
   - Include virtual playable 1-octave musical keyboard with keyboard keybindings (`A`, `W`, `S`, `E`, `D`, `F`, etc.).
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Web Audio API. Zero external sound libraries.
4. Add automated test `scripts/test-fm-synth-studio.js` validating FM modulation graph connections, parameter normalization, and ADSR timing calculations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dual-oscillator FM synthesis produces authentic retro metallic and punchy tones.
- [ ] Knobs, ADSR sliders, and XY touchpad modulate sound parameters in real-time.
- [ ] Keyboard hotkeys trigger musical notes with low latency.
- [ ] Test `scripts/test-fm-synth-studio.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/VFX]: Interactive 2D Boids Flocking Simulation with Predator-Prey Dynamics Canvas
body:
## Problem
ArcadeVerse games and backdrops feature traditional particle bursts, but lack complex emergent swarm intelligence where hundreds of autonomous entities flock organically and react dynamically to player interaction and simulated predators.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/boids-flocking.css`:
   - Fullscreen/modal canvas container with HUD controls for flock size (50 to 300 boids), visual range, separation weight, alignment weight, cohesion weight, and max speed.
2. Create modular simulation engine `assets/js/boids-flocking.js`:
   - Implement Craig Reynolds' classic boids flocking algorithm:
     - Separation: Steer to avoid crowding local flockmates.
     - Alignment: Steer towards the average heading of local flockmates.
     - Cohesion: Steer to move toward the average center of mass of local flockmates.
   - Add interactive cursor behavior:
     - Attractor Mode: Boids swarm smoothly toward the cursor.
     - Predator Hawk Mode: A simulated predator swoops through, causing the flock to scatter in panic and regroup.
   - Render aerodynamic triangular boids with glowing neon velocity trails.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/HTML5 Canvas. Zero external math/flocking packages.
4. Add automated unit test `scripts/test-boids-flocking.js` verifying vector math (magnitude, normalize, limit), flocking rule forces, and boundary wrapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hundreds of autonomous boids flock smoothly across the canvas at 60 FPS.
- [ ] Boids scatter realistically away from predator cursor and regroup via emergent cohesion.
- [ ] Sliders dynamically tune flocking parameters in real-time.
- [ ] Automated test `scripts/test-boids-flocking.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Zero protected files modified.

title: [Feature/Graphics]: Interactive 2D Canvas Cellular Automata Simulation Studio
body:
## Problem
Cellular automata (like Conway's Game of Life and Wireworld) are foundational computer science algorithms that produce mesmerizing emergent complexity from simple grid rules. ArcadeVerse lacks an interactive cellular automata sandbox.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/cellular-automata.css`:
   - High-contrast retro grid canvas interface with toolbar for Play/Pause, Step, Speed, Clear, Randomize, and Grid Zoom.
   - Preset selector menu (Glider Gun, Pulsar, Pentadecathlon, Spaceship, Wireworld Clock).
2. Create modular simulation engine `assets/js/cellular-automata.js`:
   - High-performance double-buffered Uint8Array grid representing cell states.
   - Compute next generation: B3/S23 (Conway rule) and toggleable custom rule definitions.
   - Support interactive cell drawing with mouse: click/drag to paint living cells or erase.
   - Track generation counter, living cell count, and population growth graph.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas API. Zero external dependencies.
4. Add automated test file `scripts/test-cellular-automata.js` testing neighbor count calculation, glider translation over 4 ticks, and oscillator period verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cellular automata grid updates smoothly with step, play, and speed controls.
- [ ] Drawing on grid creates active cell colonies that evolve according to rules.
- [ ] Famous pattern presets (Glider Gun, Oscillators) load and run accurately.
- [ ] Automated test `scripts/test-cellular-automata.js` passes cleanly under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Theme/UI]: 1989 Sega Genesis 16-Bit High-Contrast Metallic Chrome Arcade Theme Studio
body:
## Problem
The 16-bit era of arcade cabinets and the Sega Genesis / Mega Drive featured aggressive high-contrast metallic chrome lettering, 512-color RGB palette styling, and industrial brushed metal textures that defined 1990s gaming. ArcadeVerse currently lacks this distinctive aesthetic.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/theme-genesis-16bit.css`:
   - 16-bit color palette: Sonic Blue (`#0038ce`), Sega Metallic Chrome (`linear-gradient(180deg, #ffffff 0%, #a8a8a8 50%, #484848 100%)`), Golden Ring Amber (`#f8b800`), and Industrial Dark Carbon (`#121216`).
   - High-contrast segmented bevels and metallic drop-shadows on card borders and navigation pills.
   - Stylized 16-bit geometric grid background with subtle gradient horizon.
2. Create modular studio controller `assets/js/theme-genesis-16bit.js`:
   - Register theme with theme studio under ID `genesis-16bit`.
   - Provide toggle for "Blast Processing Speed Glow" adding dynamic pulsating energy borders to active cards.
   - Persist theme selection in `localStorage`.
3. 100% Vanilla JS/CSS3. Zero external assets.
4. Add standalone test file `scripts/test-theme-genesis-16bit.js` validating theme registration, CSS variable injection, and color token compliance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 16-bit Genesis theme applies distinctive metallic chrome styling and bold color palette across all views.
- [ ] Blast Processing visual effect toggles dynamically without lag.
- [ ] Theme registers cleanly with theme engine and persists across sessions.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-theme-genesis-16bit.js` passes under `node`.
